# Which edge will they reach first?

**They will reach the LEFT edge of the image first** — specifically the left-hand
side of the frame, at a point roughly three-quarters of the way down it (about the
same height as the bottom of the post-and-rail fence), not the bottom, top or right
edge.

## What is in the picture

Three people are riding a ground-level miniature railway (a 7¼"-gauge type
ride-on train) through a park. The train runs left-to-right across the middle of
the frame, behind a wooden post-and-rail fence and in front of a trellis fence,
a corrugated-roof shed and trees. From left to right the consist is: a long empty
maroon carriage, a low dark open-framed wagon, a small maroon locomotive, then the
three riders on the vehicles behind the locomotive.

## Why the train is heading left, not right

1. **The locomotive faces left.** Its bonnet/hood — the end carrying the two
   louvred radiator grilles — points to the left, and its small open cab with the
   flat canopy roof is at the right-hand end. A bonnet-and-cab locomotive runs
   bonnet-first, so its front end is pointed toward the left of the frame.
2. **The driver sits behind the locomotive and reaches forward (leftward) to the
   controls.** The person in the dark green top, wearing green gloves, is seated
   immediately to the right of the locomotive and is leaning forward with a hand in
   the cab on the controls. Since the locomotive is in front of them (to the left),
   they are facing left — the direction of travel. If the train were going right
   they would have to be driving backwards over their own shoulder.
3. **The order of the train supports this.** The locomotive leads, the driver's
   truck is coupled directly behind it, and the passenger vehicle carrying the other
   two riders is behind that — so the front of the train is the left-hand end and
   everything trails off to the right.
4. **The riders' posture agrees.** All three are seen from behind and are angled
   slightly toward the left of the frame, looking forward along the track in the
   direction the locomotive points.
5. **The empty carriage at the left is arranged for leftward travel too.** Its
   seat back stands at its right-hand end with the open seating area running away
   to the left of it, so anyone in it would face left; and its left-hand end is a
   plain flat headstock panel with a central round coupling boss — the leading end
   of the whole train.

## Why the left edge specifically

* The rails are plainly visible continuing away from the train toward the left,
  running out of the picture through the bottom-left area of the fence and crossing
  the left border of the frame at about 75–80% of the image height. The train has
  only a short distance of open, straight track — roughly one train-length — before
  its leading carriage crosses that edge.
* The track only drops very gently as it goes left (it comes slightly nearer the
  camera), so it leaves the side of the frame well before it could ever reach the
  bottom edge. The bottom of the picture is just open mown grass with no track on it.
* In the opposite direction the track climbs slightly away from the camera and
  disappears behind the shrubs and ferns on the right, so even a right-hand
  movement would take the train out of sight into the vegetation rather than cleanly
  to the right edge — and in any case that is the direction they have come from.
* The top edge is irrelevant: it is filled with the shed roof, the pine branches
  and the tree canopy, and the track never heads that way.

**Answer: the left edge.**
